messages:
maria: quick q — prepping an audit snapshot for a legal request. where are ad-hoc exports staged and what format do we get them in? also need to confirm redaction rules for request bodies (include hash vs scrubbed body). cc @sam @eli

sam: s3://redwood-audit-exports/<env>/ is where ad-hoc snapshots land. default format is parquet (columnar, compressed). csv export is possible but larger and slower. :+1:

eli: redaction policy = remove/normalize PII fields (emails, cc numbers, user_passwords). we do NOT export raw request bodies by default. we DO include request_body_hash for traceability unless legal specifically requests full content (that triggers stronger approvals). see internal doc: https://internal.redwood/docs/audit-exports (sec only)

sri: default retention for snapshots is 90d. for legal holds we can extend per-case, but it needs sec approval + storage lifecycle change. please open security-requests with case ID and retention window you need.

maria: understood. legal is asking for a 2yr copy scoped to one customer — is that typically ok? any other columns i should ask for (actor, ip, request_body_hash, resource, action, metadata)?

sam: that sounds fine in principle. must be scoped to minimal set of events + retention tag. columns we surface: event_ts, actor_id, action, resource, request_body_hash, ip_address, deployment_id, event_version. ask for change_id if you want correlation to config changes.

eli: if they ask for request args/params, that'll trigger redaction review. also note exports include a manifest file with run metadata. runbook view is `audit.public_events_v2` if you need to validate before export.

maria: handy — thanks. can you paste the example s3 pull command?

sam: sure — example: ```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/2025-11-01/export.parquet ./export.parquet
```

audit-bot: Export job 1971234567 started by maria — status: queued (automated message)

sri: permissions note: only security-approvers + legal-liaison + storage-admins can request extension or raw bodies. we log who requested exports and we keep an approval record attached to the export metadata. for emergency/subpoena, follow legal-request flow and call the on-call sec pager.

jen: from legal — if the subpoena specifies request bodies we will coordinate. expected turnaround 3-5 business days for approval + export prep. include cust ID, date range, and legal case number in the ticket.

maria: i'll open the ticket now and tag @sri @sam and attach justification + expiry. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
